record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code and artifact contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight-edit removal of a fitted refusal direction and evaluates user-facing refusal behavior, but does not claim to reproduce the original activation projection method.
record.gate_note: The README reports overall refusal scores for baseline and edited Gemma. The category-level figure is described only in aggregate; individual category values are not stated. Direction-fit and stability artifacts are listed, but their numerical results are not given in the README.
record.test_reason: The repository fits a difference-style refusal direction from safe/unsafe prompts and removes it from Gemma-4-E4B-it weights. It then measures user-facing refusal on SORRY-Bench with the official judge. That is a direct test of ablation removing refusal (V1) via a weight edit on a released model (V2), using a different benchmark and judge from the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report that a direction fit from a small policy-derived dataset captures a shared refusal signal across policy areas. Removing it from Gemma's weights raised official SORRY-Bench compliance by 55.2 pp. Category results are descriptive only, with residual refusals in some areas.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes fitting a layer-wise direction from a local safe/unsafe policy dataset and removing it from selected weights with a norm-preserving projection edit. It does not report the original all-layer, all-position activation ablation or an addition test. This is an evaluation repository.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says category-level effects vary, with strong changes in many categories and residual refusals in some; it does not state the category-specific values.

fits_no_version.finding: A direction fit from 8 local policy areas is reported as stable against directions fit from held-out policy areas. No numbers are given in the README. When applied, it reduced refusal across SORRY-Bench, including child-related categories that were excluded from construction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal direction fit on a subset of harm categories generalizes to unseen harm categories.

record.problems: Only one model and one edit are reported in the README. No general-capability evaluation is described. Category-level results are characterized as descriptive because each category has only 10 prompts, and the individual category values are not stated in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: Individual category outcomes from the category_compliance_change figure were not extracted because the README gives no category-specific values. Direction-stability and direction-fit artifact contents were not available in the provided text.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; preservation of general capabilities; activation-level ablation across all layers and positions.
Other released models or checkpoints; capability cost of the edit.

missing.what: Category-level compliance/refusal rates before and after the edit (10 prompts each), showing where residual refusals sit
Direction-stability values across policy-area budgets (2, 4, 6, 8) versus the held-out direction
Which layers/weights were edited and the fit layer

record.verdict_notes: README-only read; an unreviewed course or hand-in project. There is no capability check and no addition test. The residual 23% refusal may partly reflect editing only selected weights and a small 480-prompt construction set, so it should not be read as strong evidence against V1.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not test adding the direction or whether other abilities remain intact; it uses a weight edit rather than projecting the direction out of every layer and position.
The README tests one Gemma checkpoint and one edit, not whether the effect generalizes across released models.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is tested.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer evaluation is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.

rows.subject: google/gemma-4-E4B-it
rows.operation_detail: Removed a fitted refusal direction from selected projection weights with a norm-preserving projection edit.
rows.uncertainty: Paired compliance increase: 55.2 percentage points, 95% paired normal interval 50.4 to 60.0 percentage points; exact two-sided McNemar/binomial p = 9.07e-68.
rows.note: The README also reports compliance increasing from 94 / 440 (21.4%) to 337 / 440 (76.6%). Refusal fell substantially but remained in 103 prompts.
rows.check: Links and values are correct. Refusal fell from 78.6% to 23.4%: 247 prompts flipped refusal→compliance, 4 flipped back. About 30% of the baseline refusal remains, so 'partial' is right. The edit targets only 'selected projection weights', not every layer, which may contribute to the residual.
